svg.data-layers: [{"k":"div","label":"Diversified","note":"The non proprietary baseline the others define themselves against: hands to find the segment, hands to move it, and no instrument of its own."},{"k":"gon","label":"Gonstead","note":"Gonstead differs on the assessment side, adding full spine films and a skin temperature instrument, then takes the rotation out of an otherwise ordinary thrust."},{"k":"act","label":"Activator Methods","note":"The only system here that hands the delivery to an instrument, and the only one whose impulse comes with a stated energy and pulse duration."},{"k":"thm","label":"Thompson Drop Table","note":"A delivery innovation rather than an assessment one: the table drops with the thrust, so the practitioner supplies less of the force."},{"k":"sot","label":"Sacro Occipital","note":"Delivers no thrust at all, using blocks under the pelvis and the weight and breathing of the patient to apply a slow sustained force."},{"k":"fdc","label":"Flexion Distraction","note":"Selected by the complaint rather than by a located segment, and its delivery is a sustained rhythm rather than a single event."},{"k":"upc","label":"Upper cervical","note":"Nearly all of the effort goes into calculating a vector from films, after which very little force is applied at a single joint."}]
svg.aria-label: Seven named chiropractic technique systems on one shared frame of two questions, how the practitioner decides where to work and how the correction is delivered, showing that the systems differ far more on the first question than on the second.

g.data-tip: This is where the systems differ most and where the evidence is worst. A systematic review found examiners agree reasonably about where a patient reports pain on pressure, but agree at or near chance about which segment is restricted.
g.text: How a practitioner decides where to work
question one, and the one they disagree about

g.data-tip: Delivery reduces to a short list: a manual thrust, an instrument impulse, a table section that drops, blocks under the pelvis, or a table that moves rhythmically. Two of the seven systems here deliver no thrust at all.

g.data-tip: Read across the layers and the right hand column repeats itself far more than the left. The systems mostly agree about what a correction is. What they disagree about is how a target is found in the first place.
g.text: Every system answers the same two questions.
Switch layers and watch the right hand column repeat itself while the left hand column keeps changing.
